items.title: 25.2 Retrosynthesis and Synthesis of Some Compounds

source_refs.note: Topic 25.2 as printed: Examples 25.2.1-25.2.3, the cholesterol box and Quick Check 25.2 (PDF 137-139); the schemes are redrawn. Step II of Example 25.2.1 prints benzene and nitric acid (marked).

blocks.text: Disconnection at the position indicated will enable us to get synthon A and synthon B whose synthetic equivalents are also shown. While selecting synthetic equivalent molecules thus obtained, they should undergo reaction to give the target molecule.
These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., benzene and nitric acid molecule.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Step II of Example 25.2.1 prints “benzene and nitric acid” (the words of the aniline example). For ethyl acetate the synthetic equivalents are acetic acid (for synthon A, CH₃CO⁺) and ethanol (for synthon B, C₂H₅O⁻), as the scheme and the next sentence show.
For our target molecule ethyl acetate, the disconnection followed by neutralization yields acetic acid and ethanol as simpler staring materials to synthesize the TM.

blocks.alt: Step I: ethyl acetate drawn with a wavy slash on the bond between the C=O carbon and the ester oxygen, a Disconnection arrow, then the acylium ion H3C-C(=O)+ as synthon (A) plus the ethoxide ion, -O-C2H5, as synthon (B). Step II: synthon (A) is equivalent to acetic acid (SE) and synthon (B) to ethanol (SE). Synthesis: CH3-COOH + C2H5-OH, with H2SO4, gives CH3-CO-O-C2H5 + H2O.
blocks.caption: Example 25.2.1: retrosynthetic tree and synthesis of ethyl acetate (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 137-138).

blocks.text: Here we can design the synthesis of our TM by a very familiar esterification reaction between acetic acid and ethanol to get ethyl acetate.

First step of retrosynthesis here is FGI, where amino group (NH₂) is converted into nitro (NO₂) group. Because it is easy to attach nitro group on benzene by electrophilic substitution, rather than amino group by nucleophilic substitution.
In second step the disconnection of nitrobenzene was done from C—N bond, which created synthons of aryl anion (C₆H₅⁻) and nitronium (NO₂⁺) cation.
These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., benzene and nitric acid molecule.

blocks.alt: Step I: aniline (benzene with NH2) and an open arrow labelled FGI to nitrobenzene. Step II: nitrobenzene with a wavy slash on the C-N bond, a Disconnection arrow, then a benzene ring with a negative charge, synthon (A), plus NO2 with a positive charge, synthon (B). Step III: benzene (with H shown), HNO3 over and H2SO4 under the arrow, to nitrobenzene, then Sn + HCl to aniline.
blocks.caption: Example 25.2.2: retrosynthetic tree of aniline (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 138).

blocks.text: In first step the disconnection of acetophenone (TM) was done from C—C bond, which created synthons of aryl anion (C₆H₅⁻) and acylium (CH₃CO⁺) cation.
These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., benzene and acyl chloride molecule.

blocks.alt: Step I: acetophenone (benzene with C(=O)CH3) with a wavy slash on the ring-carbon bond, a Disconnection arrow, then a negatively charged benzene ring, synthon (A), plus the acylium ion H3C-C(=O)+, synthon (B). Step II: synthon (A) is equivalent to benzene (SE) and synthon (B) to acyl chloride H3C-CO-Cl (SE). Synthesis: benzene + acyl chloride, with AlCl3, gives acetophenone + HCl.
blocks.caption: Example 25.2.3: retrosynthetic tree and synthesis of acetophenone (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 138).

blocks.text: Synthesis of acetophenone can be done by reaction between benzene and acyl chloride, in the presence of AlCl₃ as catalyst, using Friedel-Craft acylation process.

blocks.title: Interesting Information
blocks.text: The landmark synthesis of cholesterol was first achieved in early 1950s by two competing groups headed each by Robert Robinson in Oxford and R.B. Woodward at Harvard. These synthetic schemes of cholesterol, had been previously predicted through biological studies.

blocks.title: Quick Check 25.2
blocks.text:
a) Why nitration of benzene is done during synthesis of aniline?
b) Phenyl ethanoate is an important molecule used in synthesis of medicines for hepatitis and various infection.
(i) Draw its retrosynthetic tree.
(ii) Write structures of its synthetic equivalents.
(iii) Design its linear synthesis.
